newsitem.title: USA: Guidant Q3 led by ICD, pacemaker gains.
newsitem.headline: Guidant Q3 led by ICD, pacemaker gains.

text.p: Guidant Corp said third quarter sales were led by record revenues in its cardiac rhythm management segment, including sales of implantable defibrillators and pacemakers.
Cardiac rhythm management sales of $144.7 million were up 21 percent over the year-ago period, the company said.

"Sales of implantable defibrillators, driven by the Ventak Mini HC and the newly introduced Ventak Mini II, continue to show rapid growth," said chief executive Ronald Dollens. "This is particularly impressive in light of recent introductions of implantable defibrillator products by our competitors."
Guidant also said pacemaker sales achieved good results versus a strong year-ago quarter.
The medical devices manufacturer, based here, on Monday reported third quarter net sales of $260.1 million, an 11 percent increase over third quarter 1995.
Foreign currency exchange rates decreased sales growth by about two percentage points, Guidant said.
Net income increased to $41.2 million, or $0.57 per share, up 47 percent over third-quarter 1995 earnings per share and ahead of Wall Street expectations by about $0.03 per share.
Shares in Guidant were up 1/4 to 49-5/8 early on Monday.
In other segments of the business, Guidant said sales worldwide of its vascular intervention products fell three percent to $320.7 million on the quarter ended September 30 versus a year ago.

"Product mix shifts toward lower priced catheter platforms, continued pricing pressure and unfavorable comparisons in atherectomy product sales impacted total (U.S.) vascular intervention performance," the company said.
Third-quarter sales of Guidant's minimally invasive systems products were $10.7 million, a 67 percent increase over the third quarter of 1995.

Gross profit on the quarter was $191 million, or 73.4 percent of sales. Operating costs were $116.3 million, or 44.7 percent of sales. Sales, marketing and general administrative costs were up nine percent over a year ago, while research and development expenses grew 17 percent, Guidant said.

"We are pleased with the momentum in our business, particularly the achievement of 47 percent net income growth and 15.8 percent after tax return on sales in the third quarter. In addition, strong cash flow in the quarter allowed us to reduce our debt from $449 million at the end of the second quarter to the current level of $397 million," said chairman James Cornelius.

Finally, Guidant added that it received a supplemental ruling from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service that will allow it to use its stock directly for acquisitions or to be sold in a secondary offering in support of acquisitions.
"We therefore expect to complete our previously announced approximately 10 million share offering near the end of this month," Cornelius said.
